description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v4.0.0-alpha.18: CORRECTION to alpha.17's release notes, plus one rule for resolving the user id -- read UPGRADE.md section 31. CORRECTION: alpha.17's notes said "deleting a role does not delete the assignment rows pointing at it (no foreign key on RoleId, only on UserId)". Both halves are wrong. MyIdentityUserRoleAssignment declares [ForeignKey("RoleId")] and it materializes as FK_MyIdentityUserRoleAssignment_AspNetRoles_RoleId with ON DELETE CASCADE from the first migration, so on a normally-migrated relational database deleting a role DOES delete its assignment rows. UserId is the one with no FK of its own; the library declares it for you in ApplyMyIdentityConstraints. If you planned a data migration believing grants survive a role deletion, re-check it. Nothing in the library changed there -- the documentation was wrong and the schema was always right. Alpha.17's behaviour change stands: removing the creation validator from a removal path was correct either way, only its motivating scenario was wrong. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: the package carried three different rules for resolving which user a principal is, duplicated across thirteen call sites -- both IMyIdentityCurrentUserAccessor leaves plus nine more production call sites (the permission decision point, seven guards and self-checks in MyIdentityUserService, and impersonation in MyIdentityAuthenticationService) all hardcoded ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier, the JWT revocation hook read NameIdentifier then fell back to sub, and the Blazor revalidating provider honoured IdentityOptions.ClaimsIdentity.UserIdClaimType. A consumer who set UserIdClaimType did not get a smaller inconsistency at the edges -- for any caller who was neither a SystemAdmin nor a TenantAdmin with a tenant, which is every delegated manager and every ordinary user, the permission decision point denied every permission check outright, because it read ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier directly and found nothing. All thirteen now read the claim type Identity is configured to emit and fall back to sub, which matters because MapInboundClaims is false so an external issuer's sub arrives un-rewritten. Under the default UserIdClaimType nothing that resolved before stops resolving; if you set a custom UserIdClaimType there are two directions -- read UPGRADE.md section 31. If you supply your own IMyIdentityCurrentUserAccessor, GetUserIdAsync() is now load-bearing at eleven internal call sites (up from three) and must agree with GetUserAsync(); a stub returning null now denies permissions and blocks self-service operations on default configuration. BREAKING: MyIdentityHttpContextCurrentUserAccessor and MyIdentityBlazorCurrentUserAccessor take IOptions<IdentityOptions> as a second constructor argument -- source- and binary-breaking for code that constructs them directly rather than through DI; recompile, and outside DI pass Options.Create(new IdentityOptions()). API may still change before stable.
